discriminatingCase.test: decoded application keeps the preceding mutable write when a later tuple is rejected
discriminatingCase.reason: The frozen applier validates each operation as it reaches it, so a leading set stays applied when a later tuple is rejected. Whole-batch pre-validation would leave the caller at its initial value, and an ingestion seam that accepted an unknown verb or a string splice index would not report those messages at all.

comparisons.scenario: unsafe prototype segments and malformed operation tuples are rejected before mutation
comparisons.test: decoded operation ingestion rejects the frozen malformed shapes before any target access

discriminatingCase.test: decoded ingestion rejects every reserved segment and never yields a partial batch
discriminatingCase.reason: A path check that special-cased only the frozen __proto__ spelling would accept constructor and prototype, which reach the same JavaScript prototype surface, and an ingest-as-you-go seam that returned the accepted prefix would hand a caller a partially validated batch; the case requires all three reserved segments and whole-batch rejection.

comparisons.scenario: mutable application mutates in place except for a root replacement, which returns a new value
comparisons.test: mutable application mutates in place while a root replacement returns a new value

discriminatingCase.test: a root replacement keeps the preceding incremental write and adopts a new root
discriminatingCase.reason: An applier that wrote the adopted replacement into the caller's value would make replacementIsNew false, and one that discarded the writes before a replacement would lose the preceding set; the case requires the caller's prior write to survive and the returned root to be a distinct container that shares the replacement payload.

comparisons.scenario: document watches and states deliver only committed frames
comparisons.test: a committed watch frame's frozen delta vocabulary matches the tracker draft and value

discriminatingCase.test: a whole-root replacement is not the delta a committed watch frame delivers
discriminatingCase.reason: A delta vocabulary that also accepted a whole-root replacement as the committed frame's shape would pass decoding while not matching the frozen two-set frame; the case requires the committed frame to be a non-base batch and the tracker's prepared replacement of the same value to differ from it.

comparisons.scenario: aborting a changed draft revokes escaped handles and leaves the committed revision unchanged
comparisons.test: aborting a prepared change revokes escaped draft handles

discriminatingCase.test: aborting a prepared change revokes escaped draft handles
discriminatingCase.reason: An implementation that refuses prepare but leaves an escaped draft handle usable would apply the escaped write and advance the revision; the case requires the settled overlay error, the aborted-preparation error, and the unchanged committed value and revision.

comparisons.test: cancelling the close caller rejects close while storage cleanup still completes

comparisons.test: cancelling a watch acquisition rejects the wait and leaves no write or partial observer

comparisons.test: the progress byte rate is the frozen 100 KiB/s constant

discriminatingCase.test: progress pacing separates a byte-rate pause from a constant interval and rounded bytes
discriminatingCase.reason: The frozen constant is the 100 KiB/s byte rate, so the pause for a 50 KiB commit is 500 ms and a 1 025-byte commit buys 10.009765625 ms. A seam that uses a fixed millisecond interval reports 100 ms for the first and a seam that rounds the bytes or the pause reports 10 ms for the second; both fail here while the bare constant assertion still passes.

comparisons.test: frozen hardware-cursor observations replay across MainScreen and AltScreen

discriminatingCase.test: ITui roots support hardware-cursor preference and IME positioning
discriminatingCase.reason: The frozen scenario observes the default hidden preference on the main screen; a root that always hides the cursor satisfies it. The ITui case separates a preference that is always hidden from one that follows the root preference and re-positions the IME cursor when the viewport scrolls.

comparisons.test: frozen hardware-cursor observations replay across MainScreen and AltScreen

discriminatingCase.test: ITui roots support hardware-cursor preference and IME positioning
discriminatingCase.reason: The toggle scenario observes the visible frame after setShowHardwareCursor(true); a setter that stores the value without re-rendering satisfies the stored state but not the frame. The ITui case separates the stored preference from the rendered cursor and its IME positioning.

comparisons.test: Program status format encodes frozen OSC 7501 fields and limits

discriminatingCase.test: Program status reply recognition accepts only the frozen query echoes
discriminatingCase.reason: A formatter that emits the frozen field order still passes if the same predicate silently accepts an unrelated OSC 7501 body. The reply-recognition case separates encoding from recognition: a status report and a color report must be rejected while all three query echoes are accepted.

comparisons.test: Program status format encodes frozen OSC 7501 fields and limits

discriminatingCase.test: Program status reply recognition accepts only the frozen query echoes
discriminatingCase.reason: The frozen scenario pins omission of an invalid app, of a non-blocked kind and of a blank message plus the base64/UTF-8 message bound; an implementation that appends every field passes a shape check but fails those rows. The reply-recognition case additionally separates formatter behavior from the reply predicate the terminal relies on.

comparisons.test: Text re-wraps at a new horizontal padding like frozen pi

discriminatingCase.test: Box padding change invalidates the render cache
discriminatingCase.reason: A Text that re-renders from scratch on every call passes the three padding transitions without carrying any invalidation. The Box cache case separates a changed padding that invalidates a cached composition from one that returns the previous frame.

comparisons.test: Text re-wraps at a new horizontal padding like frozen pi

discriminatingCase.test: Box padding change invalidates the render cache
discriminatingCase.reason: The frozen scenario observes re-wrapping at the narrowed content width; a setter that only re-clamps the visible padding keeps the previous single line. The cache case separates an invalidating setter from one that reuses the cached composition.

comparisons.test: AltScreen selection replays styled CJK cells across wrapped rows and copies frozen text

discriminatingCase.test: AltScreen selection preserves the cell range through content and focus changes
discriminatingCase.reason: The styled CJK scenario observes one drag across two wrapped rows; a highlight pass that paints the first drag and drops the range on the next frame passes it. The lifecycle case separates a stored cell range from a per-frame highlight.
